summary: Iter144 — E2E verification of 4 new Crisis Commander features (Connector Health, Board Auto-Present on real close, Header Tidy Up / More overflow menu, Auto-SITREP cadence + folded cron). Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_iter144_crisis_ext.py — 7/7 PASS covering (a) GET /crisis/connectors/native returns last_received+count per vendor; (b) GET /crisis/connectors/health returns {health:{vendor:{last_received,count}}}; (c) POST /crisis/ingest/native/splunk with real webhook secret → last_received flips to a timestamp and count increments by 1 (mirrored under /connectors/health); (d) Board Auto-Present: created a throwaway CRISIS case, PATCHed status:'Closed' → snapshot created (non-revoked token) + Timeline event 'Board snapshot auto-prepared on close; emailed to N director(s)' (source=Auto-Present) written; (e) demo:true cases correctly SKIP auto-present (no Auto-Present event); (f) sitrep_schedule_hours PATCH persists for 0/4/12/24 via GET /crisis/cases/{ref}; (g) run_scheduled_sitreps imported and invoked in-process against org_id → wrote EXACTLY ONE 'Auto-SITREP posted to leadership chat' timeline event (source=Auto-SITREP), with _post_chat_alert monkey-patched to no-op so no live Teams/Slack post fired. Frontend: logged in as jblan2026, dismissed onboarding, /app/cyber-crisis-commander loaded cleanly (cyber-crisis-commander-page). Header at 1920px shows only inline primaries — crisis-demo-toggle, crisis-scenario-start, crisis-refresh-btn, crisis-executive-brief-btn (Executive Brief) and crisis-more-btn — one row, no wrap. crisis-more-btn opens crisis-more-menu containing crisis-share-snapshot-btn, crisis-ingest-servicenow-btn, crisis-email-brief-btn, crisis-brief-cadence (Auto-brief select, 12h), crisis-sitrep-cadence (Auto-SITREP select, Off), crisis-walkthrough-btn — all visible + clickable. Post-Incident Review + Report Pack correctly hidden for the current Open case. Incident Command tab shows crisis-native-connectors with all 5 vendor cards, each rendering crisis-native-health-<vendor>: crowdstrike + splunk show a live green pulse + 'Live · last received … · N event(s)' after the ingest test, sentinel/servicenow/generic show grey 'No events received yet'. All 13 tabs (including Board View) cycle cleanly, no white screen. Only 2 unrelated 400s from a background poller (pre-existing, noted in iter143). Cleanup: all TEST_ITER144 cases + snapshots deleted; CRISIS-0002 preserved as Open with sitrep_schedule_hours=0.
critical_code_review_comments: crisis_commander.py update_case (L304-308): _auto_present_board is wrapped in a bare 'except Exception: pass'. If snapshot creation or email fails, the PATCH still returns 200 with the case marked Closed but neither a snapshot nor a timeline event is written — the operator has no visible signal the auto-present failed. Recommend logging the exception (logger.exception) and/or writing a 'Auto-Present failed' Communication event so the failure is auditable.

run_scheduled_sitreps (L2605-2645): the throttle check uses sitrep_last_sent_at and skips cases where hours have not elapsed, but the timeline event + sitrep_last_sent_at is written UNCONDITIONALLY after _post_chat_alert returns — even if the Teams/Slack post silently failed (the try/except swallows). Consider writing the timeline event only when at least one channel POST returned success, otherwise the audit trail can claim a SITREP was posted when it wasn't.

connector health map is not org-scoped in the response schema documentation — verified in code the query is {'org_id': org_id}, so isolation is correct, but the collection crisis_connector_health should have a compound (org_id,vendor) unique index to prevent duplicate rows under concurrent ingests (currently relies on upsert filter only). Recommend await db.crisis_connector_health.create_index([('org_id',1),('vendor',1)], unique=True) inside _ensure_indexes.

_auto_present_board (L2652): FRONTEND_URL fallback is an empty string, producing a relative link like '/crisis-snapshot/<token>' inside the board email. Directors clicking that from an email client will get a broken link. Should fall back to the request host or a hard-required env value.

Snapshot revoke on re-close: _auto_present_board revokes ALL prior non-revoked snapshots for the case before minting a new one when the existing snapshot is expired — but if a director already has the old link bookmarked, that becomes silently invalid. Consider extending expires_at on the existing token instead of revoking+reissuing.

seed_data_creation: During the test run: 1 TEST_ITER144 splunk native ingest (updated connector_health rows for splunk + crowdstrike from prior runs); 3 throwaway CRISIS cases (close/autopresent, demo-skip, sitrep-cadence) — ALL deleted along with their events/snapshots/actions/participants/recovery/obligations rows. Auto-Present real close: 1 director email was sent to the real admin/executive/owner mailboxes (this is by design — the feature spec accepts one email per closed test case). Auto-SITREP: _post_chat_alert was monkey-patched to no-op so NO live Teams/Slack post fired. CRISIS-0002 sitrep_schedule_hours confirmed reset to 0.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 4 iter144 features are green end-to-end. GET /crisis/connectors/native now returns last_received (ISO string or null) + count (int) per vendor; GET /crisis/connectors/health returns {'health': {<vendor>: {last_received, count, last_title}}}. Case PATCH accepts sitrep_schedule_hours (0/4/12/24 in UI, 0..168 in schema). Board Auto-Present is triggered inline in update_case ONLY when status flips to 'Closed' AND case.demo is not truthy. Auto-SITREP is folded into the hourly-overdue-digest cron via background_tasks (still 5 crons total). To test Auto-SITREP safely in-process: `import self_scan; self_scan._post_chat_alert = <no-op>` before calling `crisis_commander.run_scheduled_sitreps(org_id=...)`. Test file test_iter144_crisis_ext.py handles Mongo cleanup automatically via _delete_case_via_mongo helper.
